title: Chef John’s Pumpkin-Braised Pork
description: Chef John’s pumpkin-braised pork takes a cooking pumpkin and fills it with seasoned pork shoulder and hard cider to make this easy, slow-baked recipe.
ingredients: 2 cups hard apple cider, or more as needed

steps.text: Cut pork into large chunks; place in a bowl. Add shallots, salt, rosemary, black pepper, fennel seeds, thyme, and cayenne pepper; mix thoroughly. Cover pork with parchment paper. Refrigerate to let flavors develop, 8 hours to overnight.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Add flour to pork; toss to coat. Heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook pork in 2 batches until browned, about 3 minutes per side.

Slowly cut top off pumpkin by inserting the tip of a knife at a 45-degree angle into top; cut all the way around to remove “lid” with stem. Scrape seeds and fibers off bottom of lid and inside pumpkin using a large spoon or ice cream scoop.
Line bottom of a baking pan with parchment paper; place pumpkin on top. Stuff pumpkin with browned pork; pour in cider. Cover with pumpkin lid.

Bake in the preheated oven until pork is very tender, about 4 hours, adding a little more cider after a few hours, since it evaporates a lot. Remove from oven; rest. Brush pumpkin with some rendered fat from bottom of the pan.

Scoop pork onto serving plates; cut pumpkin into pieces to serve. Combine remaining rendered fat with cooking liquid from inside pumpkin; rest 3 to 5 minutes. Skim most fat off top of sauce; spoon over pork.

video.description: If you're looking for a fun, and very seasonably appropriate way to cook some pork shoulder, I can't think of a better, or more beautiful one, which is why I really hope you give this a try soon. Season the pork any way you want.
